data.gender_notes: Bhim is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Bhim is a name derived from Sanskrit and means 'powerful' or 'strong'. In Hindu mythology, Bhim is the second eldest of the Pandava brothers, known for his immense strength and courage. The name Bhim carries the meaning “Powerful, Strong” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bhim usually hope their child will grow to embody powerful, strong and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength and courage in the face of adversity.
data.etymology: Bhim belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Powerful, Strong.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bhim total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: Bhim is a prominent figure in Hindu mythology and represents strength, power, and courage. He is also known for his unwavering loyalty to his brothers and devotion towards his wife, Draupadi. The name Bhim has been commonly used in India for centuries and continues to be a popular name among Hindus.
data.spiritual_significance: Bhim is not just a symbol of physical strength but also represents inner strength and moral courage. In Hinduism, the divine quality of Bhim serves as an inspiration for individuals to work towards overcoming obstacles, remaining faithful to their duty, and staying committed to their spiritual pursuits despite challenges.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bhim, named after Bhima the powerful Pandava brother in Mahabharata, symbolizes strength, courage, and loyalty. His name is a reminder to overcome challenges with unwavering determination and unyielding spirit.

historical_references.reference: Bhim is the second of the two sons of Vidura, a wise and just sage in the Mahabharata epic. The name Bhim is derived from the Sanskrit word 'bhima', which means 'terror' or 'strong'.

Bhim is also known as Bhima Kartikeya, the elder brother of the great warrior Bhima in Hindu mythology. He was born to King Vibhishana of Lanka and his consort Tulasi, who was also a manifestation of the goddess Tulasi. Bhima Kartikeya is considered an incarnation of Lord Subrahmanya, the warrior god.
